component.name: PyNetboot
component.summary: Create bootable USB drives from ISO files

description.p: PyNetboot is a cross-platform tool for creating bootable USB drives from ISO files.
It allows you to create bootable Live USB drives for a variety of Linux distributions, as well as other operating systems and utilities.
Features:

ul.li: Download ISO files from various distributions automatically
Create bootable USB drives from existing ISO files
Supports Windows, macOS, and Linux
Persistent storage support for Live USB drives

description.p: PyNetboot is a Python rewrite of UNetbootin, originally created by Geza Kovacs.
Adds Manjaro, and updates Linux Mint and Zorin OS.

ul.li: Manjaro 26.0.4 in Xfce, KDE Plasma and GNOME editions
Linux Mint 22.3 now offers both Cinnamon and MATE
Zorin OS 18.1 Core and Lite, replacing the older 18 revision
All of these verify their download against the publisher's checksum

description.p: Fixes copying files to the drive on Windows.

ul.li: Formatting a drive briefly removes its letter. Writing began before the drive came back, so every file failed. It now keeps its original letter and is waited for

description.p: Protects a drive that cannot be released at the end of a write.

ul.li: If the drive is still in use when the write finishes, its contents are no longer deleted during tidying up. This affected Linux and macOS
A drive that cannot be released now says so, instead of failing silently

description.p: Fixes writing a drive on Windows.

ul.li: Files are now written to the drive itself. Preparing the drive failed at the last step, and the path it would otherwise have used was a temporary folder rather than the drive

description.p: The log can be opened at any time, and failures explain themselves.

ul.li: The Log button now works while a drive is being written, which is when it is most useful
When a drive cannot be written, the reason is shown instead of a bare "Preparation failed"
On Windows, the lack of administrator rights is reported before the drive is touched rather than part-way through

description.p: Starts much faster on Windows.

ul.li: Listing drives no longer takes about three seconds. It asked Windows through a helper program that is slow to start; it now asks the system directly, which is immediate. This applied at start-up and again on every refresh
Checking an empty card reader no longer raises a "there is no disk in the drive" message

description.p: Uses your desktop's own file chooser on Linux.

ul.li: Choosing where to save an image now opens the desktop's usual file chooser, with its shortcuts and recent folders, instead of a plain built-in one
The chooser opens on the folder currently shown in the field
Desktops without one continue to use the built-in chooser. Windows and macOS were already using their own

description.p: Fixes writing a drive on Windows.

ul.li: Images can be unpacked again on Windows. Every helper program was reported missing there, so no method could be used and unpacking always failed
Console windows no longer flash up while a drive is being written
Dialogs now carry the application icon instead of a generic one

description.p: Fixes a crash on start-up on Windows, and the Windows application icon.

ul.li: Windows 11 no longer ships the tool this used to list drives, which made the application fail on start-up with an unrelated message. Drives are now listed the supported way, with the old method kept for earlier Windows versions
The application icon now appears on the Windows window and task bar instead of a generic one

description.p: Applies the recent Linux fixes to macOS and Windows.

ul.li: On macOS the drive is now given a partition table, where before the filesystem was written straight over the boot record and the drive would not boot
Failures on macOS and Windows now report their cause instead of failing silently
Missing system tools are reported before the drive is modified, rather than part-way through

description.p: Asks for your password once for the whole operation.

ul.li: Writing a drive now prompts for authentication a single time, instead of once for each privileged step
If authentication cannot be held open, each step asks separately as before, so the write still completes

description.p: Fixes copying files to the drive, and asks for your password less often.

ul.li: The drive is now mounted so that your user account can write to it. Every file previously failed to copy with a permission error, because the drive was mounted by the administrator account instead
Preparing the drive now asks for your password once rather than for each step

description.p: Records much more detail in the log, making a failed write easier to diagnose.

ul.li: The download, extraction, copy and bootloader steps each report their size, duration and outcome
The target drive's size, model and mounted partitions are recorded before anything is written to it
Copying an empty image is now reported as a failure instead of quietly producing an unbootable drive

description.p: Makes a silently empty extraction impossible.

ul.li: Unpacking an image is now confirmed to have produced files. An extraction tool that exited successfully without unpacking anything used to be taken at its word, producing a drive that could not boot but reported a completed install
If one extraction method produces nothing, the next one is tried instead of giving up

description.p: Fixes creating a bootable USB drive.

ul.li: The target drive is now given a partition table before formatting. Previously the whole disk was formatted and the boot record was then written over the filesystem's own boot sector, so the drive did not boot
The bootloader is installed to the partition and the boot record to the disk, as they require
The Flatpak now ships parted, and the disk tools are reachable at runtime

description.p: Fixes formatting a USB drive on Linux.

ul.li: Partitions on the target disk are now unmounted before formatting, which previously failed with "Device or resource busy"
Formatting errors now report the underlying cause
The software centre now shows the application name, icon and license

description.p: Renamed the project from UNetbootin to PyNetboot.

ul.li: New application ID, command name and package name
Existing settings are preserved
